title: Prompt tuning: learned prompts instead of written ones

videos.script: Every prompt in this course so far was written by a person, in words. {{words}} The model never reads those words directly. It turns each token into a list of numbers first. {{vectors}} So here is a strange idea. What if the prompt were never words at all? {{idea}} Prompt tuning puts a few lists of numbers in front of the input, and trains them. {{train}} The model itself does not change. Only those few numbers are adjusted, example by example, until the answers improve. {{frozen}} What comes out is a prompt nobody wrote and nobody can read. {{unreadable}} It works for one model, on one task, and it needs things most people do not have: the model's weights and a set of examples. {{needs}} In this lesson you see what a soft prompt is, and where it sits between a written prompt and fine-tuning. {{between}} By the end you will know why, with a hosted model, you will probably never do it, and why it is still worth knowing. {{why}}
